candidates: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 - Background legacy writes use the request context and get cancelled when the request returns.. Each goroutine builds its context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, where `ctx` is the incoming request context. The handler returns right after starting the goroutine, and the API server then cancels the request context. The legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection usually fails with `context canceled` or never runs, so legacy storage silently falls out of sync. That defeats the "safe measure" the request describes. The same pattern is at lines 110, 135 and 163. Fix: start from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`, which keeps the request values but drops its cancellation, then add the 10s timeout.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 - A failed storage Create is recorded as a legacy duration.. When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. Unified-storage failures therefore show up in the legacy metric and are missing from the storage metric. Use `recordStorageDuration` here.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 - A successful storage Delete records the object name as the metric's kind label.. `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. Successful deletes are then labelled under the wrong kind, and every distinct object name creates a new label value, so the metric's cardinality grows without bound. Pass `options.Kind`.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 - A failed storage Update is recorded as a legacy duration.. When `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`, so storage failures are counted under the legacy metric. Use `recordStorageDuration`.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 - Legacy DeleteCollection timing is recorded as a storage duration.. The goroutine runs `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` and then calls `d.recordStorageDuration`. Legacy timings and errors are mixed into the storage metric, and the legacy metric never sees delete-collection. Use `recordLegacyDuration`.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 - Legacy write failures are no longer logged.. The old code logged every legacy write error. The new goroutines (Create, Update, Delete, DeleteCollection) only pass `err != nil` to a duration metric and drop the error itself. When the async write to legacy fails, nothing records which object failed or why, so the drift cannot be diagnosed or repaired. Log the error inside each goroutine, e.g. `log.Error(err, "unable to create object in legacy storage")`.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 - Legacy Create reads the same `obj` concurrently with the response path.. The goroutine passes the original `obj` to `d.Legacy.Create` while the request goroutine returns `created`. Storage implementations often mutate `obj` in place (resourceVersion, UID, timestamps) or return the same pointer. The response encoder and the legacy store then read and write the same object at the same time, which is a data race. Legacy may also receive storage-assigned metadata such as resourceVersion and reject the create. Pass a `DeepCopyObject()` of the input to the goroutine.
